subtitle: Per-symbol coverage of the C <stdint.h> header. SHIPPED as re_std's dstdint.h (inc/re_std/c/cstdint/dstdint.h), which is also the C++ face's source (cstdint.hpp re-exports each name as re_std::). Two backends, chosen by RE_STD_CFG_STDINT_BACKEND (AUTO prefers the platform): PLATFORM includes the platform's <inttypes.h>, or its <stdint.h> alone, and completes what it leaves out; OWN defines every name from the compiler's predefined macros (__INT32_TYPE__ and its family), or derives it from <limits.h> where those are missing too. IDENTITY: every type is the exact type the platform's header uses. ABSENT, NOT APPROXIMATED: a family is present exactly when its limit macro is defined. Verified by dstdint.c (compile-time claims) and t_dstdint.c (format round trips): 184/184 checks at C99, C11, C17 and C2x on both backends (gcc 13, x86_64 Linux). C23's width macros are the remaining gap.
legend_blurb: <stdint.h> provides the fixed-width integer types (exact, minimum, fastest, pointer-holding, greatest), their limits, the limits of the other integer types and the integer constant macros.

symbols.name: int8_t / uint8_t
symbols.notes: OPTIONAL in the standard: only where the implementation has a type of exactly 8 bits with no padding bits. Present exactly when INT8_MAX is defined -- the test the standard prescribes -- and absent, never approximated, where the target has no such type. Own backend: a typedef of the compiler's __INT8_TYPE__ / __UINT8_TYPE__, the type the platform's own header uses, so overloads, _Generic selections and printf formats agree with it, and the system header may be included as well.
symbols.failure_reason: Ships at C99 under ISO strictness, below the workbook's C90 floor. Floor question, not a coverage gap: C90 has no <stdint.h>, and the one measured obstacle to a C90 path is syntax -- every // comment in dstdint.h and config.h is an error under -std=c89 -pedantic-errors. Where // is accepted (gcc -std=gnu89, measured; other C90 compilers that take // as an extension, unmeasured) the conformance harness passes on both backends: 184/184 checks on the platform's headers, 169/169 on the header's own definitions. See the (meta) C90-floor item.

symbols.name: int64_t / uint64_t
symbols.notes: OPTIONAL in the standard. Several ABIs spell it `long long` -- LLP64 Windows, every 32-bit target, and macOS although `long` is 64 bits there -- so it exists only where `long long` does (RE_STD_HAS_LONG_LONG), and no other 64-bit type stands in, since that would break identity. RE_STD_HAS_INT64 records the answer when the header is first included: INT64_MAX can appear later in the same unit from another system header (on glibc, <netinet/in.h>), so a test of it can change its answer. Own backend: a typedef of the compiler's __INT64_TYPE__ / __UINT64_TYPE__, the type the platform's own header uses, so overloads, _Generic selections and printf formats agree with it, and the system header may be included as well.

symbols.name: int_leastN_t / uint_leastN_t (N = 8, 16, 32, 64)
symbols.notes: Mandatory in the standard, but the own backend leaves the 64-bit pair out where the build cannot spell its type (no `long long`). Derived from <limits.h> where the compiler predefines nothing: widths exact, but where two standard types share a width the lower-ranked one is chosen (`int` over `long`), which the platform may not do.

symbols.name: int_fastN_t / uint_fastN_t (N = 8, 16, 32, 64)
symbols.notes: No ABI fixes these, and a compiler's predefined macros can disagree with the C library: Clang predefines `short` for int_fast16_t on Linux, where glibc declares `long`. The own backend therefore declares the family only where it knows which <stdint.h> the platform uses (the compiler's own, or a C library whose choice dstdint.h section 2.4 records) and leaves it out elsewhere, with all of its limits and formats: the family is present or absent as a whole.

symbols.name: intptr_t / uintptr_t

symbols.name: INTN_C / UINTN_C (N = 8, 16, 32, 64)
symbols.notes: Each expands to an integer constant expression suitable for #if with the type the promotions give int_leastN_t. Own backend: the suffix comes from the spelling class of the type itself (none, U, L, UL, LL or ULL), not from the platform's limit macros, which may spell it another way. Clang 20 and older, freestanding, on the platform backend, give UINT8_C and UINT16_C the wrong type (WG14 DR 209, fixed in Clang 21); the own backend is the way out.

symbols.name: INTN_WIDTH / UINTN_WIDTH, and the LEAST, FAST, INTPTR and INTMAX widths
symbols.notes: The width in bits of each type: C23 (earlier in TS 18661-1, behind __STDC_WANT_IEC_60559_BFP_EXT__). Not provided: the platform backend passes them through where a C23 library has them, and the own backend never defines them. Back-portable to C99 at no risk -- each width is a fixed fact of a type the header already describes, and the own backend knows it.
symbols.failure_reason: NOT IMPLEMENTED. C23 addition; re_std has no equivalent yet. Tracked on the <stdint.h> roadmap entry.

symbols.notes: C23. As the type widths: fixed facts, back-portable wherever the matching limit is defined.

symbols.name: __STDC_VERSION_STDINT_H__
symbols.notes: The library's own statement that its <stdint.h> is C23's (202311L). re_std should not define it: it would claim a conformance the platform has not given. A back-port of the C23 additions should answer through a re_std feature macro instead.
symbols.failure_reason: Deliberately not provided: a conformance claim belongs to the platform. Listed so the C23 surface is complete.
